goals.title: A crane the friends walk like a hamster wheel
goals.critique: This is new, and it is the first candidate where the friends are part of the machine: their own weight drives a device built from wood and rope, so who you put in the wheel is a real choice with real numbers, and pulleys trading force for speed is honest physics that works by what it is. The wheel spinning backwards with Pinchy still sprinting, while the top course slides off, is a clip people would send, and the road starts with the plainest proof (a stone over one, two and four pulleys) before any friend climbs in. The weak side is that the friends' minds are again a list of scripted distractions (tired, gull, butterfly), which risks the player reacting to random interruptions rather than reading them, and stacking stones by friction is familiar from many building and physics toys, so the tower half carries less than the wheel half.

goals.title: Build the clock that wakes the island
goals.critique: This is new, and the idea that the whole island lives by a time the player made is a real conceit: a pendulum, escapement and weight train are a true device whose behaviour comes from its parts, and a chipped tooth or a heated rod are failures you can find. But its feedback is a week long: a pendulum a finger too long shows only as friends drifting out of step over days, mostly while the player is not watching, so the minute-to-minute play shrinks to nudging a bob and waiting, close to a slider with a delay. The noon wake-up is funny once, but it is the slow sum of an error rather than something the player causes in the moment, and a ticking clock is pretty to watch rather than a clip people pass around.
